notes:
PASSED on the fake backend only: python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/pythondev0__zscan-optical-system --backend fake exited 0 on 2026-11-17 (G1-G7 and G9 pass; G8 is warn only, with G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE). The evidence state is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json authored_by kind model, reviewed_by null); no human reviewed or tested it, no camera was attached, the upstream clone was never imported or run, and no hardware run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names PythonObjectDriver and lists two entry symbols (camera:ThorlabsCamera and stage:AerotechStage). The package uses a direct Driver over camera:ThorlabsCamera because the primary output is an image artifact (cap.sensing.image.v1), which the config-only PythonObjectDriver command table cannot publish. One package has one native class, so this package serves the camera only; the Aerotech stage (stage.py:9) is NOT COVERED, including move_absolute, get_position, disable and the z-scan synchronization loop. The stage is a separate device and control path, not a resource of the camera. The card role driver-pack does not change the SDK rule that one package has one native device; the stage is left to a separate package.

MOCK PATH: the card prefers a fake; the clone ships no simulator or tests. fake.py is a source-shaped in-memory stand-in, not a recording, with only the members the upstream class has (h_cam, width, height, mem_ptr, mem_id, capture_image, release). It returns an 8x8 placeholder frame (all numbers marked placeholder); the real frame is 1280x1024 Mono8 (README.md:18, camera.py:43-46). The action reports the actual captured array dimensions; the reads report the constructor's 1280x1024 allocation. The fake is not hardware evidence.

ACTION: cap.sensing.image.v1 capture calls native capture_image (is_FreezeVideo(IS_WAIT) and get_data), validates a two-dimensional Mono8 frame (integers 0..255, equal row lengths, 1..8192 pixels per side), encodes a lossless 8-bit grayscale PNG with mhs.pixels.encode_png_rows, and publishes it through the endpoint-owned artifact store. Without an artifact store the action fails MHS.DEVICE.NOT_READY before the native capture. The default store per-artifact bound is 2 MiB; the 1280x1024 Mono8 PNG fits it, and a deployment can raise the store bound up to 16 MiB. NOT COVERED: the optional cap.sensing.image.v1 exposure_ms, format, width and height inputs; the upstream class has no exposure, format or ROI setter, so declaring them would invent an interface. The camera selector input is accepted and ignored because one camera is configured.

LIMITS: no Limit is declared because the only served input is a string camera selector and the camera exposes no numeric command. No site-limits.example.json is shipped. G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is the expected consequence: the suite awards CL2 because SAFE-014 has no limit path to probe, while every other CL3 conformance test passed. Adding a numeric input only to satisfy SAFE-014 would invent an interface the upstream does not have.

SAFETY: the declared risk is R0 (data-only camera capture; MHS/spec/04-safety.md lists camera capture as R0), the card floor. No @estop and no estop_physical_ref are declared: the only native stop-shaped call is release (camera.py:69-72), which frees the image memory and exits the camera and cannot be undone without constructing a new ThorlabsCamera. The endpoint's software e-stop latches and refuses further captures (the G6 e-stop test reports software_only); a native is_FreezeVideo call already in progress has no timeout in the clone and is not aborted by this driver, so no physical stop is claimed. release is the endpoint teardown. No re-arm, reset or fault-clearing action is declared.

HARDWARE: the .native:connect factory constructs the upstream ThorlabsCamera(device_id=...) from camera.py under a deployment-provided source_root or from the operator's PYTHONPATH. It needs pyueye and the IDS uEye SDK (README.md:85); the card's pip command only installs the Python requirements. The hardware path was not run. The upstream constructor does not check the return codes of is_SetColorMode, is_AllocImageMem or is_SetImageMem (camera.py:39-47), so a deployment must verify that the camera is usable after construction.

PROVENANCE: all 15 Facts cite README.md, camera.py, zscan.py, stage.py or requirements.txt at 114c2838f5c3cc7a5a211ed34b38f0745c386f74; G4 passes. No extension ids were used; cap.sensing.image.v1 is a catalogue class, so no catalogue_requests entry is needed. G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is the only warning. check-report.json is generated by the gate and is not part of the package; the digest above is the gate digest line of the last run.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Model review checked both card entries against the pin, every Fact, native.py, image publication and the fake-only R0 stop semantics. native.py now uses the source SDK calls with checked initialization, allocation, capture and release statuses, preventing a failed freeze from publishing old image memory and avoiding upstream lifecycle stdout prints. driver.py and facts.md now distinguish unchecked upstream calls from successful acquisition and handle nonfinite pixel conversion; test_driver.py exercises initialization failures, failed-freeze receipts and cleanup with SDK-shaped stubs. reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json were regenerated, and the fake gate and strict collector pass with contract_checked evidence; no upstream module, vendor SDK or device was imported or run. For the human reviewer: Only the camera is served. AerotechStage is excluded: its constructor enables the axis (stage.py:29-30), and wait_for_motion_done only sleeps (50-57), so this review establishes neither stage stopping nor settling. The checked adapter uses the pinned camera module for SDK dependencies; IS_WAIT is still blocking and cannot be aborted by the R0 software latch. Stub checks and the 8 x 8 fake frame do not validate the SDK, hardware timing or the real 1280 x 1024 acquisition. RESULT.json retains the author record; no signature was added.
